grading.s_criteria: Proper confluences, clear confirmations, sniper entries leading to TP and a high RR (3.5RR and higher). T-0012: 'it met our criteria (CH+DEMAND+ Avoiding inducement) + Very good RR'. Target clarity counts: T-0016 is S over a higher-R A 'because ... our confirmations could help us identify our TP level much easier' (a key level built by many retests).
grading.a_criteria: A good setup executed well, one step short of S: a better entry or a stronger target would have made it S (T-0001, T-0006).
grading.b_criteria: Decent R:R but few confluences: 'it could be a risky execution'. T-0009: 'Setup B because of FVG ignorance but decent confirmations'.
grading.c_criteria: A setup taken without the full process, 'regardless of win' (T-0003: only the 1m timeframe).
grading.d_criteria: A poor trade plus a mistake: 'D would definitely be a poor trade+mistake'.

process.top_down: Top Down Analysis: start from a main (higher) timeframe, zoom into lower timeframes to identify key levels, and go to the lowest timeframes for execution (trader, 2026-09-26). The worked example (T-0013, 2026-10-13): the weekly for the trend and the CH, the 1D for liquidity, support/resistance and supply/demand levels, the 4H for the support range and the demand that formed the CH, then the 1H or 30M for confirmations and the execution.

terminology.CHoCH: Change of character. Bullish CHoCH requires a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
terminology.extreme demand level: The red box: the full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest.
terminology.extreme supply level: Mirror of extreme demand, at the higher high.
terminology.invalidation %: Distance from entry to stop, in percent.
terminology.lower low: A candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). Vice versa for a higher high.
terminology.reclaim: Price back above a swept level, holding it as support; secondary entry.
terminology.confluences: Liquidity sweep; strong bullish momentum + volume; inducement; potential resistance level.
terminology.Top Down Analysis: Main timeframe first, then lower timeframes for key levels, then the lowest timeframes for execution.
terminology.key level: Support/resistance drawn from a wick; valid after multiple reactions. A range, not a single price: 'it's not a specific price, it's a range depending on how much price reacts' (T-0013).
terminology.deviation: Price moves through a level and fails to hold: a fakeout.
terminology.retest: Price returns to a broken level and tests it from the other side.
terminology.reclaim-retest-accept: Long sequence: level reclaimed, retested from above, and held.
terminology.CH: The trader's chart label for CHoCH.
terminology.I became the liquidity: My stop sat in the liquidity that price swept before reversing (T-0004).
terminology.divergence: Regular bullish: price LL, RSI HL. Regular bearish: price HH, RSI LH. Hidden bullish: price HL, RSI LL. Hidden bearish: price LH, RSI HH. Just a confluence; the higher the timeframe, the stronger.
terminology.supply/demand level: Drawn where price created a CH (bearish: supply, bullish: demand), stronger with an FVG: 'we draw supply demand levels which form a FVG +CH'.
terminology.mitigation: Price returning into a supply/demand level. Unmitigated = high probability; the more it mitigates, the weaker it becomes. T-0007's supply is the example; a zone traded through and reclaimed with a CH is a reclaim level, not mitigation (T-0006).
terminology.FVG: Fair value gap. Strengthens the supply/demand level whose move left it.
terminology.inducement: Equal highs/lows: resting liquidity (equal lows = liquidity resting below, T-0001). 'AVOID Inducements at all costs'.
terminology.level validity: S/R levels and trendlines: at least 3 reactions preferred. Not for S/D levels (fewer mitigations = stronger).
terminology.reaction: Not knowable in advance: a level is key if traders react to it. A touch that rejects, a break-retest-continue, or a deviation (break, retest, fail, level lost again). Mostly deviations, so the retest is traded for continuation.
terminology.equal highs/lows: No fixed tolerance; they may take longer to form. Still a liquidity level likely to be swept. Near a stop: 'we either be careful of a potential liquidity sweep/deviation or placing our SL above swing highs. The opposite goes on longs' (2026-10-17). T-0014's retest highs were not equal highs in the trader's reading. With equal highs/lows at the trade: wait for the sweep and the deviation, enter on the retest (2026-10-19); the bot's tolerance is calibrated from the trader's $$ marks (0.2% counted, BERA; 0.56% did not, AAVE). A sweep alone means nothing; a reversal must follow. A sweep with no reversal ('has no power') is continuation: the setup and the levels close to it fail (2026-10-20).
terminology.potential CH (30m): A 30m candle closes below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (bearish), or above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (bullish).
terminology.S setup: Proper confluences, clear confirmations, a sniper entry that runs to TP, and a high R:R (about 3.5R; a rough guide) (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0007.
terminology.grades: S, A, B, C, D. S-B tradeable, C maybe, D avoided. Criteria for each in grading (all stated by 2026-09-28).
terminology.4H candle range: The range of the impulsive candle that made the high/low (cyan lines). Inside it = consolidation. A pullback must CLOSE beyond its opposite end.
terminology.fake CH: A lower-timeframe CH the next timeframe up does not confirm: '30M CH' while on the '1H there wasn't any CH, it was just a pullback on a consolidation range' (T-0011). Same as NOT CH.
terminology.Breaker Block (BB): A fresh level where a solid support broke and was reclaimed; with an FVG on the 30M it is a continuation entry: 'new FVG+Breaker Block (BB) at 30M where reclaimed support level as well' (T-0013). Built: 'you can see the mini pullback which created inside the zone, went lower and then reversed higher forming an FVG' (2026-10-14).
terminology.Premium Level: Above the 0.5 of the Fib on the weekly swing ('yes exactly', 2026-10-14): 'The higher price is (Premium Level) the more we consider looking for Day trading because it has potential to go lower to mitigate FVGs or demand levels' (T-0013). 'since we are above 0.5 we are looking for day trading, maybe for swing as well if we see some extra confirmations but its risky.'
terminology.discount level: Below the 0.5 of the weekly Fib; '61.8-78.6-88.6 we can focus on swings as well' (2026-10-14). The Fib sits on the weekly swing points ('Fibonacci retracement was on weekly swing point'): BTC, 57,733.48 to 87,318.63: 0.5 = 72,526.06, 0.618 = 69,035.01, 0.786 = 64,064.70, 0.886 = 61,106.19.
terminology.Avoiding inducement: Placing the limit at the zone beyond the equal highs/lows, never at them, so the inducement is swept into the zone first. One of the S criteria: 'CH+DEMAND+ Avoiding inducement' (T-0012).
terminology.front run: Price moves toward the target without retesting the entry level first; the limit is cancelled: 'we got front runned so we cancel our entry, since there wasn't any retest' (T-0011). For the bot: cancel when price makes a new low beyond the previous low before the retest ('The ideal option would be b when price makes new low so it's likely for price to get invalidated', 2026-10-14).
terminology.NOT CH: A break of a level inside a candle range. Consolidation, not a change of character (T-0008).
terminology.pullback: From a high, price must break and CLOSE below the low of the candle range, read on the HTF (4h); otherwise it is consolidation. A 1h pullback inside a 4h candle range is not a 4h pullback (trader, T-0008).
terminology.early execution: Entering before the setup's confirmation or location is reached: 'setup was good but executed early' (T-0004); 'mistake here was early execution' (T-0009).
terminology.ignoring FVG: Taking a trade with an unmitigated FVG left behind it: 'I ignored FVG on the left so I knew that this execution was risky' (T-0009).
terminology.middle of nowhere: Price away from any HTF zone: 'price was in the middle of nowhere. I'd focus at 0.27-0.31 zone to consider looking for longs' (T-0009).
terminology.counter-trend: Trading against the HTF trend (T-0007: short at ATH levels). Graded like any other setup; just a bit riskier (trader, 2026-09-27).

other.label: Other (describe in journal; promote to its own tag once it recurs)

choch.label: CHoCH (change of character)
choch.definition: Bullish CHoCH requires a candle CLOSE above the last lower high; a wick through does not count.

inducement.label: Inducement
inducement.definition: Equal lows = liquidity resting below (equal highs: above). A confluence only when price sweeps it into the zone. 'AVOID Inducements at all costs': never enter at one (trader, 2026-09-27).

extreme_demand.label: Extreme demand level
extreme_demand.definition: The red box: the full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest (trader, 2026-09-26).

reclaim.label: Reclaim (support reclaim)
reclaim.definition: Price closes back above a level it swept (in T-0001 the former inducement / equal lows) and holds it as support. Used as a secondary entry.

extreme_supply.label: Extreme supply level
extreme_supply.definition: Mirror of extreme demand: the full wick-to-wick range of the high-volume candle at the higher high.

key_level.label: Key level (S/R)
key_level.definition: Support/resistance level (or trendline) drawn from a wick. Valid after multiple reactions, at least 3 preferred (trader, T-0003 and 2026-09-27).

deviation.label: Deviation (fakeout)
deviation.definition: Price moves through a level and fails to hold beyond it (trader's words: 'deviation/fakeout').

retest.label: Retest
retest.definition: Price returns to a level it just broke or lost and tests it from the other side.

divergence.label: RSI divergence
divergence.definition: Regular bullish: price lower low, RSI higher low. Regular bearish: price higher high, RSI lower high. Hidden bullish: price higher low, RSI lower low. Hidden bearish: price lower high, RSI higher high. A confluence only; any timeframe, the higher the stronger (trader, 2026-09-27).

demand_level.label: Demand level (S/D)
demand_level.definition: Drawn where price created a bullish CH; stronger with an FVG; high probability when not retested (mitigated), weaker with every mitigation (trader, 2026-09-27).

supply_level.label: Supply level (S/D)
supply_level.definition: Drawn where price created a bearish CH; stronger with an FVG; high probability when not retested (mitigated). T-0005 is the trader's example.

candle_range.label: 4H candle range (candle range)
candle_range.definition: The high-to-low range of the impulsive candle that made the swing (the trader's cyan lines). Price that stays inside it is consolidation. A pullback needs a CLOSE beyond the opposite end (below a bullish candle's low, above a bearish candle's high); a break of a level inside the range is NOT a CH (trader, T-0008; the same rule on the 30m in T-0004).

fvg.label: Fair value gap (FVG)
fvg.definition: A gap left by an impulsive move. A supply/demand level that formed an FVG with its CH is stronger; T-0001's demand kept an unfilled FVG (trader, 2026-09-27).

breaker_block.label: Breaker block (BB)
breaker_block.definition: The trader's 30M 'BB + FVG' box: a fresh level where a solid support was broken and reclaimed, used for a continuation entry without a 30M CH once the HTF CH is in: 'FVG and BB breaking a solid support level seemed a solid choice to enter for a trade as a continuation on fresh level' (trader, 2026-10-13). Built: 'you can see the mini pullback which created inside the zone, went lower and then reversed higher forming an FVG' (trader, 2026-10-14): a mini pullback inside the zone, a move below it, then a reversal through it that leaves an FVG.

stop_in_liquidity.label: Stop in the liquidity beyond an obvious swing, where the valid entry forms ('I became the liquidity')

false_ch.label: Treated a break inside a candle range (consolidation) as a CH: 'NOT CH'

early_execution.label: Early execution: entered before the setup's confirmation or location was reached ('setup was good but executed early')

ignored_fvg.label: Ignored an unmitigated FVG left behind the entry ('I ignored FVG on the left')

premature_exit.label: Exited before the plan's exit criteria

cut_winner_early.label: Cut winner / took profit too early

cancelled_front_run.label: Cancelled a limit that price ran away from without a retest: 'we got front runned so we cancel our entry, since there wasn't any retest'

avoided_inducement.label: Avoided the inducement: the limit sat at the zone beyond the equal highs/lows, which were left to be swept into it ('Avoiding inducement')

A.label: Good loss
A.meaning: Valid setup, controlled risk, plan followed; the trade simply failed.
A.lesson: Keep the process. Do not change the strategy because of one normal loss.

B.label: Strategy failure
B.meaning: Setup looked valid but the strategy may underperform in these conditions.
B.lesson: Investigate the conditions under which the strategy fails.

C.label: Execution error
C.meaning: Strategy valid, execution deviated from the plan.
C.lesson: Fix execution rather than the strategy.

D.label: Invalid setup
D.meaning: The trade should never have been taken.

E.label: Information deficiency
E.meaning: Reasonable decision on available information; later information invalidated the thesis.
E.lesson: Only add a rule if the missing information was knowable and recurs. Do not overfit one loss.

meta.name: Key level S/R: reclaim-retest-accept / deviation-retest
meta.summary: Trader, with T-0003: "Found a key level Support/Resistance waiting for price to react multiple times to confirm its valid so either i would take long for reclaim-retest-accept or short in case of losing the level again, which it did." Demonstrated once, as a 1m scalp without top-down analysis. Scalp top-down: 30m-1h, 15m, 1m-5m (trader, 2026-09-27).

1.0.source: Stated by the trader with T-0003 (SOLUSDT 1m scalp), 2026-09-26
1.0.direction: Both. Long on reclaim-retest-accept; short when the level is lost again (deviation) and retested.
1.0.level_definition: Key support/resistance level drawn from a wick. It is valid once price has reacted to it multiple times. T-0003: tapped, lost, reclaimed and lost again. The trader's chart note reads (translated from Greek): "Possible resistance point. For validity, ideally we see extra resistances/supports."
required_conditions: A key level validated by multiple reactions.
Long: the level is reclaimed, retested from above, and accepted.
Short: the level is lost again (the reclaim was a deviation), then retested from below.
confirmation: Multiple reactions at the level
Retest of the level from the other side
confluences: Red line: key level drawn from a wick, tapped multiple times

entry_models.reclaim_retest_accept: Long: on the retest after the level is reclaimed and accepted.
entry_models.deviation_retest: Short: on the retest from below after the level is lost again (T-0003).

1.0.stop_model: Beyond the latest swing before price broke the level, in case it reclaims the level. For a short, the latest high before the break (T-0003: 85.7453, the 20:32 high before the 20:33 break).
1.0.leverage_model: Isolated margin, within the 50% margin-loss rule. Higher leverage when the invalidation % is small (T-0003: 0.24% stop, 20x).
1.0.context: The trader called T-0003 risky because no top-down analysis was done: only the 1m chart was used, so higher-timeframe levels that could invalidate the setup were not checked.

management.invalidation: Stop beyond the latest swing before the break (see stop_model).

do_not_trade_when: Best target gives less than 2.5R (the trader's general rule).
open_questions: 1. How many reactions make a level valid: two, three, more?
2. How is the target chosen? T-0003 exited at 84.9409 (2.94R).
3. For scalps, which higher timeframes does the top-down analysis use?
4. Fees: are they inside the 1% risk? With a 0.24% stop, trading fees are a large share of 1R (see T-0003).

5. T-0003 timing: price traded through the 84.9409 target at about 21:01-21:04, about 24 minutes after entry, but you report 45 minutes. Was the TP a resting order, or did you close by hand at about 21:25?

meta.name: Supply/Demand + Price Action / Market Structure (liquidity confluences)
meta.summary: Trader's main strategy, in their words: "supply/demand level and price action/market structure, adding few confluences with liquidity levels". The long-side sequence was demonstrated in T-0001. The trader confirmed that every rule mirrors for shorts from supply (2026-09-26).

1.0.source: Stated by the trader with T-0001 (AAVE 4H), 2026-09-26
required_conditions: Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high. A wick or move through it without a close does not count.
confirmation: Bullish Reversal (4H)
Extreme demand level
confluences: Liquidity sweep
Strong bullish momentum + volume
Inducement (equal lows = liquidity resting below)
Potential resistance level (used for the target)
1.0.entry_model: Primary: long at the extreme demand level. Secondary (used in T-0001 when the primary was missed): long on the reclaim of the swept inducement level (former equal lows) as support.
1.0.target_model: Next resistance level. In T-0001: the wick + higher-low level (yellow line).

1.1.source: Trader's answers, 2026-09-26 (follow-up to T-0001). Clarifies v1.0; no rule changed (CHG-001).
market_structure: Lower low: a candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). A wick below without a close is not a lower low.
Higher high: a candle must CLOSE above the previous high (its wick). ('vice versa')
Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
required_conditions: Bullish CHoCH on the 4H, close-based (see market_structure).
confirmation: Bullish Reversal (4H)
Extreme demand level (the red box)
confluences: Liquidity sweep
Strong bullish momentum + volume
Inducement (equal lows = liquidity resting below)
Potential resistance level (used for the target)

zones.extreme_demand: "The red box." In T-0001 it spans about 85.61 to 88.05, which matches the wick-to-wick range (about 85.73 to 88.00) of the lowest candle at the lower low, within about 0.1. The exact construction rule is pending (open question 3).

entry_models.extreme_demand: Primary: long at the extreme demand level (the red box).
entry_models.reclaim: Secondary: long when price reclaims the swept inducement level (former equal lows) as support. Used when the primary entry was missed (T-0001).

1.1.stop_model: At the level where the setup is invalidated: a return there means the move was a deviation or fakeout. Trader's words: "invalidated setup - possible deviation/fakeout". The mechanical placement is pending (open question 1). T-0001: 87.59, inside the red box, about 1.2 above the sweep low (86.40).
1.1.target_model: Next resistance level. High R:R is sought: "Hunting good RR setups is important." T-0001: the yellow line, 4.57R planned. No minimum R:R stated (open question 5).
1.1.leverage_model: Chosen from the entry-to-stop distance. T-0001: stop 3.14% (trader's figure) -> 10x. Leverage does not change the 1% risk; it sets the margin posted and the liquidation distance. The mapping rule and margin mode are pending (open question 4).

management.invalidation: Stop at the invalidation level (see stop_model).

open_questions: 1. Stop placement, mechanically. T-0001's stop (87.59) sat inside the red box, about 1.2 above the sweep low (86.40). Is it below the reclaim candle, a fixed point inside the zone, below the sweep wick, or something else?

2. Which lows count for the close-below rule? Read literally, it turns 4H structure bearish before T-0001's entry: Apr 18-19 closes fell below the post-CHoCH swing lows (about 103.04 and 97.08), and the Apr 20 candle closed at about 87.12, below the equal lows. Is only the major low (the lower low at the red box, about 85.73) protected, with smaller lows treated as internal structure or inducement?
3. Red box construction: is it the full wick-to-wick range of the lowest candle at the lower low?
4. Leverage: what rule maps stop distance to leverage (3.14% -> 10x), and do you use isolated or cross margin?
5. Is there a minimum R:R below which you skip a setup?
6. Do all rules mirror for shorts (supply zones, bearish CHoCH by a close below the last higher low)?

1.10.timeframe_alignment: A lower-timeframe CHoCH counts only when the 15m-30m structure confirms it. On the 30m, a potential CH is a 30m candle that closes below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (bearish) or above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (bullish) (trader, 2026-09-27). Until then a 5m CHoCH is only 30m consolidation (T-0004: "the 5M CH was a 30M consolidation"). This is the candle-range rule (see market_structure) applied on the 30m. For a 4h zone executed on the 1h, the CH line is drawn on both charts (T-0006: about 56.00); the 1h is used only after the 4h shows a true CH (T-0008: "If there was a pullback and would see a true CH for potential short, we could jump to (2) 1H time frame").
market_structure: Lower low: a candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). A wick below without a close is not a lower low.
Higher high: a candle must CLOSE above the previous high (its wick).
Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
Bearish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE below the last higher low (mirror, confirmed). T-0007: after a new higher high, a lower low broke the previous higher low.

Candle range (4H candle range): price inside the range of the impulsive candle that made the high is consolidation. A pullback needs a CLOSE below that candle's low (above a bearish candle's high for the mirror). A break of a level inside the range is NOT a CH (trader, T-0008: 'to form a pull back from that price it had to break the lowest line and close below').

The candle range is read on the HTF first (4h): its high and low are the cyan lines. A lower-timeframe move inside it can be a 1h pullback, but it is not a 4h pullback; only a 4h close beyond the range changes the story, and only then may a trade be considered (trader, 2026-09-27).
Continuation in a bearish environment (lower highs, lower lows): after a pullback, a new lower low must CLOSE below the previous low including its wick; mirror for bullish (trader, 2026-09-27).
T-0001: the market was bearish; the 4H reversal (bullish CHoCH) was the confirmation, with confluences (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.10.trend_context: Counter-trend trades are graded like any other setup; they are just a bit riskier (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0007: short at ATH levels while the bias was bullish, "definitely worth the risk" at 4.12R. An FVG in the trend's direction between entry and target is a warning: price may close the gap or continue (T-0007).

zones.definition: A supply/demand level is drawn where price created a CH: a bearish CH leaves a supply, a bullish CH leaves a demand. It is stronger when the move also left an FVG. Trader, 2026-09-27: "we draw supply demand levels which form a FVG +CH". The zone is the level that created the reversal, not a sweep candle (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0005: the level that created the reversal left the new supply; the short was its retest. T-0007: the level that created the CH, close to the swing high, so it could also act as an inducement: that is why the stop went above the swing high.
zones.freshness: "A supply/demand level is high probability when it's not retested (mitigated)." "The more a supply/demand level mitigates the weaker it becomes." T-0001's demand kept an FVG that was not filled (trader, 2026-09-27). Unlike support/resistance, where more reactions make a level stronger. A zone that price trades through and then reclaims with a CH is a reclaim level, not a mitigated zone (T-0006: "there wasn't any mitigation, it was a reclaim level + CH"). T-0007's supply is the trader's mitigation example.
zones.extreme_demand: The full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: 85.61 to 88.05. Massive volume: the volume bar "exploded", much more than 2x; the trader asks not to focus on this (2026-09-27).
zones.extreme_supply: Mirror: the full wick-to-wick range of the high-volume candle at the higher high.

1.10.inducements: "AVOID Inducements at all costs" (trader, 2026-09-27). Equal lows/highs are resting liquidity (AAVE, T-0001: the equal lows were the inducement). There is no fixed tolerance for "equal": they may take longer to form and still count as a liquidity level likely to be swept (trader, 2026-09-27). Price is expected to sweep them into the zone: do not enter at them, and do not leave the stop just beyond them (T-0004: "I became the liquidity").

1.10.entry_timing: After a CH, the limit goes at the zone on the timeframe the setup is read on, the longer the better: "the longer time frame the better, the best example is T-0007" ("In that case, entry was on 4H chart"). Candle size after the CH is not a criterion: "Ignore small and weak candles" (trader, 2026-09-28). T-0006: the green box (demand) + the bullish CH were enough, "so I didn't have to jump to LTF". An unfilled limit is cancelled when price reaches the TP level first ("I cancel limit when hasnt filled when price reaches TP level", 2026-09-27).
1.10.split_entries: Optional. On the 1h or 30m, find extra unmitigated demand levels + FVGs and split the size across limit orders: "Usually it's going to be until 3 limit orders. 1 order only = 1% (Full size), 2 orders= 0,5% each, 3 orders= 0,3% (it's okay if it's 0.9% total risk) and yes SL and TP are the same for all orders" (trader, 2026-09-28). Supply mirrors. An unfilled order is cancelled like any limit when price reaches the TP first. T-0006: an order at the unmitigated 1h FVG under the green box "wouldnt be wrong if I did"; the trader's reason for skipping it (that losing the green box would weaken and invalidate the setup) is NOT a rule: "Don't copy me on last sentence". Sizing: tj size --add-entry.

entry_models.extreme_demand: Primary (long): at the extreme demand level.
entry_models.extreme_supply: Primary (short): at the extreme supply level (mirror).
entry_models.supply_level: Short at a supply level created by a bearish CH: sell limit at the unretested supply (T-0007), or the short on its first retest (T-0005, the level that created the reversal).
entry_models.demand_level: Mirror of supply_level: long at a demand level created by a bullish CH, on its first retest.
entry_models.reclaim: Longs when price reclaims a swept level or a demand it traded through and retests it as support; shorts mirror. T-0001: a swept level, used when the primary entry was missed. T-0006: a reclaim level + CH (the 4h demand traded through, reclaimed, and the long taken on its retest).

1.10.stop_model: Placed where the setup is invalidated. Longs: below the demand zone, the swing low, or a liquidity level. Shorts: above the supply zone, the swing high, or a liquidity level (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: at a liquidity level from the left that had been reclaimed as support. A return there means price reverses lower or goes into consolidation, and the setup is invalid. Not just beyond an obvious swing high/low: that is liquidity price sweeps before reversing, and the valid entry forms exactly there (trader, T-0004: "valid short position would be exactly on where I put my SL"). The stop goes beyond the zone that forms from the sweep (T-0005: above the new supply). T-0006: "placed SL on the last swing low it created" (51.02, under the Aug 2 sweep low of about 51.12). T-0007: "Our SL would obviously be our latest swing high in case level gets invalidated" (7,818.4, about 0.8 above the ATH that created the bearish CH). How close: "just very close to that swing point or demand/supply level" (trader, 2026-09-28): no fixed buffer. T-0006 about 0.10 under the low (0.18% of price), T-0007 about 0.8 over the high (0.01%), T-0009 about 0.0005 under the higher low (0.14%). The rule (trader, 2026-09-27: "yes exactly"): the stop goes a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH: a bit lower than the swing low for longs, a bit higher than the lower high / swing high for shorts. T-0006 and T-0007 are the examples. T-0004's stop sat beyond a high whose 5m CH the 30m never confirmed, so that high was liquidity. At liquidity levels (equal highs/lows, trendlines) wait for the break-sweep and the reclaim, then take the retest (T-0001, AAVE).
1.10.target_model: Opposing levels. "Both are ideal but it's more preferable to hunt strongest levels" (trader, 2026-09-27): the strongest opposing level (e.g. the next supply/demand zone; T-0006: the 70.70 supply) is preferred over the first level that gives at least 2.5R, which is acceptable. High R:R is hunted: 1:3 minimum preferred, 1:2.5 accepted. T-0006's order was 66.10 (3.41R): "I was happy with RR". T-0007: the key S/R level at 7,574 (4.12R).
1.10.risk_model: 1% of equity per trade, always. Fees are inside the 1% (trader, 2026-09-27); the bot will count them separately. No daily stop, no pause after losses, no cap on the number of open trades: "there's no stopping we stick to the plan. only 1% risk we ignore frequency. there's no pause" (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.10.leverage_model: Isolated margin. Leverage is chosen from the stop distance so that the loss on the posted margin at the stop (stop distance % x leverage) is 50-60%: "always aim for 50-60% at the stop" (trader, 2026-09-28), because "margin call occurs on 80%" (2026-09-27). Above 60% is a breach; below 50% is only short of the aim (the loss at the stop is still 1%). Liquidation must also sit beyond the stop: on tight stops the aim's top can liquidate first (0.6% stop: 100x is 60%, but a 0.5% maintenance rate liquidates first above about 91x; tj size prints the cap). T-0001: 3.14% x 10x = 31.4%. T-0006: 6.28% x 7-8x = 44-50.3%. T-0007: 0.615% x 20x = 12.3%. No fixed leverage cap: "with invalidation we can adjust leverage so we won't be close to margin call (80%). for example having 7% invalidation we can use until 7-8X" (trader, 2026-09-27). Leverage never changes the 1% risk.

management.invalidation: Stop at the invalidation level (see stop_model).

do_not_trade_when: Best target gives less than 2.5R.
The lower-timeframe CHoCH is not confirmed on 15m-30m (T-0004).
The entry would be at an inducement ('AVOID Inducements at all costs').

A high-impact (red) USD event on ForexFactory is due within the next hour: no new entry, and resting orders are cancelled. Entries resume 1 hour after the release: 'they can resume after 1H after manipulation could stop. anything resting gets cancelled too' (trader, 2026-09-28). Open trades are kept (2026-09-27).
checklist: 1. HTF key level or supply/demand zone identified (4h): drawn from a CH, stronger with an FVG, fresh (unmitigated) preferred.
2. Liquidity swept into the zone (equal highs/lows or an obvious swing).

3. CHoCH by candle close, beyond the range of the impulsive candle that made the swing, read on the HTF (4H candle range): a break inside that range is NOT a CH, even if the 1h shows a pullback (T-0008). On the 30m: a close below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (shorts) / above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (longs); a 5m CHoCH alone does not count.
4. Entry at the zone (supply for shorts, demand for longs), not at a lower-timeframe CHoCH below/above it.
5. Stop a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH (beyond the zone too); never beyond a swing whose CH is unconfirmed, which is liquidity (T-0004).
6. Margin loss at the stop 50-60% of isolated margin (never above 60%) with liquidation beyond the stop, and best target >= 2.5R (3R preferred; the strongest level preferred).
7. No entry at an inducement: equal highs/lows are liquidity to be swept into the zone.
8. No red USD event on ForexFactory within the next hour or released within the last hour (new entries; resting orders are cancelled for that window).

1.11.stop_model: Placed where the setup is invalidated. Longs: below the demand zone, the swing low, or a liquidity level. Shorts: above the supply zone, the swing high, or a liquidity level (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: at a liquidity level from the left that had been reclaimed as support. A return there means price reverses lower or goes into consolidation, and the setup is invalid. Not just beyond an obvious swing high/low: that is liquidity price sweeps before reversing, and the valid entry forms exactly there (trader, T-0004: "valid short position would be exactly on where I put my SL"). The stop goes beyond the zone that forms from the sweep (T-0005: above the new supply). T-0006: "placed SL on the last swing low it created" (51.02, under the Aug 2 sweep low of about 51.12). T-0007: "Our SL would obviously be our latest swing high in case level gets invalidated" (7,818.4, about 0.8 above the ATH that created the bearish CH). How close: "just very close to that swing point or demand/supply level" (trader, 2026-09-28): no fixed buffer. T-0006 about 0.10 under the low (0.18% of price), T-0007 about 0.8 over the high (0.01%), T-0009 about 0.0005 under the higher low (0.14%). The rule (trader, 2026-09-27: "yes exactly"): the stop goes a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH: a bit lower than the swing low for longs, a bit higher than the lower high / swing high for shorts. T-0006 and T-0007 are the examples. T-0004's stop sat beyond a high whose 5m CH the 30m never confirmed, so that high was liquidity. At liquidity levels (equal highs/lows, trendlines) wait for the break-sweep and the reclaim, then take the retest (T-0001, AAVE).
1.11.target_model: Opposing levels. "Both are ideal but it's more preferable to hunt strongest levels" (trader, 2026-09-27): the strongest opposing level (e.g. the next supply/demand zone; T-0006: the 70.70 supply) is preferred over the first level that gives at least 2.5R, which is acceptable. High R:R is hunted: 1:3 minimum preferred, 1:2.5 accepted. T-0006's order was 66.10 (3.41R): "I was happy with RR". T-0007: the key S/R level at 7,574 (4.12R).
1.11.risk_model: 1% of equity per trade, always. Fees are inside the 1% (trader, 2026-09-27); the bot will count them separately. No daily stop, no pause after losses, no cap on the number of open trades: "there's no stopping we stick to the plan. only 1% risk we ignore frequency. there's no pause" (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.11.leverage_model: Isolated margin. Leverage is chosen from the stop distance so that the loss on the posted margin at the stop (stop distance % x leverage) is 50-60%: "always aim for 50-60% at the stop" (trader, 2026-09-28), because "margin call occurs on 80%" (2026-09-27). Above 60% is a breach; below 50% is only short of the aim (the loss at the stop is still 1%). Liquidation must also sit beyond the stop: on tight stops the aim's top can liquidate first (0.6% stop: 100x is 60%, but a 0.5% maintenance rate liquidates first above about 91x; tj size prints the cap). T-0001: 3.14% x 10x = 31.4%. T-0006: 6.28% x 7-8x = 44-50.3%. T-0007: 0.615% x 20x = 12.3%. No fixed leverage cap: "with invalidation we can adjust leverage so we won't be close to margin call (80%). for example having 7% invalidation we can use until 7-8X" (trader, 2026-09-27). Leverage never changes the 1% risk.

management.invalidation: Stop at the invalidation level (see stop_model).

do_not_trade_when: Best target gives less than 2.5R.
The lower-timeframe CHoCH is not confirmed on 15m-30m (T-0004).
The entry would be at an inducement ('AVOID Inducements at all costs').

Price is in the middle of nowhere: no demand/supply level or key level at the entry, whatever the confluences. 'when we are in a middle of nowhere, it's more preferable not to execute. there wasn't any demand there or key level, even though there were confluences later on' (trader, 2026-09-28; T-0009).

A high-impact (red) USD event on ForexFactory is due within the next hour: no new entry, and resting orders are cancelled. Entries resume 1 hour after the release: 'they can resume after 1H after manipulation could stop. anything resting gets cancelled too' (trader, 2026-09-28). Open trades are kept (2026-09-27).
checklist: 1. HTF key level or supply/demand zone identified (4h): drawn from a CH, stronger with an FVG, fresh (unmitigated) preferred.
2. Liquidity swept into the zone (equal highs/lows or an obvious swing).

3. CHoCH by candle close, beyond the range of the impulsive candle that made the swing, read on the HTF (4H candle range): a break inside that range is NOT a CH, even if the 1h shows a pullback (T-0008). On the 30m: a close below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (shorts) / above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (longs); a 5m CHoCH alone does not count.
4. Entry at the zone (supply for shorts, demand for longs), not at a lower-timeframe CHoCH below/above it.
5. Stop a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH (beyond the zone too); never beyond a swing whose CH is unconfirmed, which is liquidity (T-0004).
6. Margin loss at the stop 50-60% of isolated margin (never above 60%) with liquidation beyond the stop, and best target >= 2.5R (3R preferred; the strongest level preferred).
7. No entry at an inducement: equal highs/lows are liquidity to be swept into the zone.
8. No red USD event on ForexFactory within the next hour or released within the last hour (new entries; resting orders are cancelled for that window).

When we get confirmation we execute hunting extreme demand levels or FVGs" (trader, 2026-09-28). T-0006's entry was decided on the 4h (the green box + the bullish CH); the 1h showed the detail.

1.12.timeframe_alignment: A lower-timeframe CHoCH counts only when the 15m-30m structure confirms it. On the 30m, a potential CH is a 30m candle that closes below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (bearish) or above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (bullish) (trader, 2026-09-27). Until then a 5m CHoCH is only 30m consolidation (T-0004: "the 5M CH was a 30M consolidation"). This is the candle-range rule (see market_structure) applied on the 30m. For a 4h zone executed on the 1h, the CH line is drawn on both charts (T-0006: about 56.00); the 1h is used only after the 4h shows a true CH (T-0008: "If there was a pullback and would see a true CH for potential short, we could jump to (2) 1H time frame").
market_structure: Lower low: a candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). A wick below without a close is not a lower low.
Higher high: a candle must CLOSE above the previous high (its wick).
Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
Bearish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE below the last higher low (mirror, confirmed). T-0007: after a new higher high, a lower low broke the previous higher low.

Candle range (4H candle range): price inside the range of the impulsive candle that made the high is consolidation. A pullback needs a CLOSE below that candle's low (above a bearish candle's high for the mirror). A break of a level inside the range is NOT a CH (trader, T-0008: 'to form a pull back from that price it had to break the lowest line and close below').

The candle range is read on the HTF first (4h): its high and low are the cyan lines. A lower-timeframe move inside it can be a 1h pullback, but it is not a 4h pullback; only a 4h close beyond the range changes the story, and only then may a trade be considered (trader, 2026-09-27).
Continuation in a bearish environment (lower highs, lower lows): after a pullback, a new lower low must CLOSE below the previous low including its wick; mirror for bullish (trader, 2026-09-27).
T-0001: the market was bearish; the 4H reversal (bullish CHoCH) was the confirmation, with confluences (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.12.trend_context: Counter-trend trades are graded like any other setup; they are just a bit riskier (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0007: short at ATH levels while the bias was bullish, "definitely worth the risk" at 4.12R. An FVG in the trend's direction between entry and target is a warning: price may close the gap or continue (T-0007).

grading.trade: S, A and B are tradeable; C maybe; D avoided: 'we can consider trading S,A,B,C trading setups. We would avoid D setups and maybe C ones as well' (trader, 2026-09-27).
grading.S: "Having proper confluences, clear confirmations, sniper entries leading to TP and a high RR (3.5RR and higher)". The 3.5R is a rough guide: "it doesnt matter if that's 3.5R it could be slightly less" (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0007 (4.12R) was graded S; the avoided POL short (T-0008, 3.40R) "would be perfectly S" had a true CH formed.
grading.A: A good setup executed well, one step short of S. T-0001: "would be A because I missed extreme demand level but I got the reclaim support level ... it would be S if I would get extreme demand and get higher RR". T-0006: "would be A because I executed well but had to let it reach supply level so it would be an S".
grading.B: "B setup would be anything with decent RR but few confluences, which means it could be a risky execution" (trader, 2026-09-28). T-0009: "Setup B because of FVG ignorance but decent confirmations where could lead to good RR" (-1R).
grading.C: A setup taken without the full process, whatever the result. T-0003: "would be C because I focused only on 1M time frame regardless of win".
grading.D: "D would definitely be a poor trade+mistake" (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0004: "it's D setup because it executed poorly (mistake) setup was good but executed early" (trader, 2026-09-28): a good setup can be a D when the execution is the mistake. What made it D rather than B: "T-0004 execution was on 5M when on 30M there wasn't any CH (On T-0004 leverage was 20X invalidation was low) that was the reason why it was a D setup. Poorly executed." The confirmation itself was missing on the confirming timeframe; T-0009 (B) had a real CH.

required_conditions: CHoCH on the 4H in the trade's direction, close-based (see market_structure).
confirmation: Reversal on the 4H (bullish for longs, bearish for shorts)
Extreme demand level (longs) / extreme supply level (shorts)
Demand reclaimed after being traded through, then retested (T-0006)
Supply/demand level not yet retested: limit order placed at it (T-0007)
confluences: Liquidity sweep
Strong momentum + volume in the trade's direction
Inducement swept into the zone (equal lows below for longs, equal highs above for shorts). Never trade the inducement itself (see inducements).
Potential opposing level (used for the target)
Divergence at the swing (see divergence). A confluence only.
Fair value gap (FVG) left by the move that created the zone (trader, 2026-09-27).
Key S/R level with many reactions as the target (T-0007: the red ray at 7,574)

zones.definition: A supply/demand level is drawn where price created a CH: a bearish CH leaves a supply, a bullish CH leaves a demand. It is stronger when the move also left an FVG. Trader, 2026-09-27: "we draw supply demand levels which form a FVG +CH". The zone is the level that created the reversal, not a sweep candle (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0005: the level that created the reversal left the new supply; the short was its retest. T-0007: the level that created the CH, close to the swing high, so it could also act as an inducement: that is why the stop went above the swing high.
zones.freshness: "A supply/demand level is high probability when it's not retested (mitigated)." "The more a supply/demand level mitigates the weaker it becomes." T-0001's demand kept an FVG that was not filled (trader, 2026-09-27). Unlike support/resistance, where more reactions make a level stronger. A zone that price trades through and then reclaims with a CH is a reclaim level, not a mitigated zone (T-0006: "there wasn't any mitigation, it was a reclaim level + CH"). T-0007's supply is the trader's mitigation example.
zones.extreme_demand: The full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: 85.61 to 88.05. Massive volume: the volume bar "exploded", much more than 2x; the trader asks not to focus on this (2026-09-27).
zones.extreme_supply: Mirror: the full wick-to-wick range of the high-volume candle at the higher high.

1.12.inducements: "AVOID Inducements at all costs" (trader, 2026-09-27). Equal lows/highs are resting liquidity (AAVE, T-0001: the equal lows were the inducement). There is no fixed tolerance for "equal": they may take longer to form and still count as a liquidity level likely to be swept (trader, 2026-09-27). Price is expected to sweep them into the zone: do not enter at them, and do not leave the stop just beyond them (T-0004: "I became the liquidity").

divergence.regular_bullish: Price lower low, indicator higher low: buy.
divergence.regular_bearish: Price higher high, indicator lower high: sell (T-0007: 7,793.9 -> 7,817.6 with RSI 81.1 -> 70.5).
divergence.hidden_bullish: Price higher low, indicator lower low: buy.
divergence.hidden_bearish: Price lower high, indicator higher high: sell.
divergence.timeframe: Most timeframes work; the higher the timeframe, the stronger (trader, 2026-09-27).
divergence.reading: Swings on the RSI and on the chart are read on wicks. The RSI length is irrelevant (trader, 2026-09-27).
divergence.source: Reference chart the trader supplied to memorize, 2026-09-27 (four panels: regular and hidden, bullish and bearish).

1.12.entry_timing: After a CH, the limit goes at the zone on the timeframe the setup is read on, the longer the better: "the longer time frame the better, the best example is T-0007" ("In that case, entry was on 4H chart"). Candle size after the CH is not a criterion: "Ignore small and weak candles" (trader, 2026-09-28). T-0006: the green box (demand) + the bullish CH were enough, "so I didn't have to jump to LTF". An unfilled limit is cancelled when price reaches the TP level first ("I cancel limit when hasnt filled when price reaches TP level", 2026-09-27).
1.12.split_entries: Optional. On the 1h or 30m, find extra unmitigated demand levels + FVGs and split the size across limit orders: "Usually it's going to be until 3 limit orders. 1 order only = 1% (Full size), 2 orders= 0,5% each, 3 orders= 0,3% (it's okay if it's 0.9% total risk) and yes SL and TP are the same for all orders" (trader, 2026-09-28). Supply mirrors. An unfilled order is cancelled like any limit when price reaches the TP first. T-0006: an order at the unmitigated 1h FVG under the green box "wouldnt be wrong if I did"; the trader's reason for skipping it (that losing the green box would weaken and invalidate the setup) is NOT a rule: "Don't copy me on last sentence". Sizing: tj size --add-entry. Fills: the stop sits beyond every order, so it is reached only after all of them fill: "it's impossible to hit SL when only 1 of 3 orders filled". R is counted on the full 1R: "if 1 order of 3 fills and reaches TP, for example 3RR it's going to be a profit of 0.9R (On trading we will count $ not only RR)" (trader, 2026-09-28). Leverage: one setting for every order, from the first order's stop: "our first limit order must not exceed 60%. if invalidation is 6% we can get 10X leverage. since we used 10X leverage on first order, we are going to use the same leverage on the rest" (trader, 2026-09-28).

entry_models.extreme_demand: Primary (long): at the extreme demand level.
entry_models.extreme_supply: Primary (short): at the extreme supply level (mirror).
entry_models.supply_level: Short at a supply level created by a bearish CH: sell limit at the unretested supply (T-0007), or the short on its first retest (T-0005, the level that created the reversal).
entry_models.demand_level: Mirror of supply_level: long at a demand level created by a bullish CH, on its first retest.
entry_models.reclaim: Longs when price reclaims a swept level or a demand it traded through and retests it as support; shorts mirror. T-0001: a swept level, used when the primary entry was missed. T-0006: a reclaim level + CH (the 4h demand traded through, reclaimed, and the long taken on its retest).

1.13.entry_timing: After a CH, the limit goes at the zone on the timeframe the setup is read on, the longer the better: "the longer time frame the better, the best example is T-0007" ("In that case, entry was on 4H chart"). Candle size after the CH is not a criterion: "Ignore small and weak candles" (trader, 2026-09-28). T-0006: the green box (demand) + the bullish CH were enough, "so I didn't have to jump to LTF". An unfilled limit is cancelled when price reaches the TP level first ("I cancel limit when hasnt filled when price reaches TP level", 2026-09-27).
1.13.split_entries: Optional. On the 1h or 30m, find extra unmitigated demand levels + FVGs and split the size across limit orders: "Usually it's going to be until 3 limit orders. 1 order only = 1% (Full size), 2 orders= 0,5% each, 3 orders= 0,3% (it's okay if it's 0.9% total risk) and yes SL and TP are the same for all orders" (trader, 2026-09-28). Supply mirrors. An unfilled order is cancelled like any limit when price reaches the TP first. T-0006: an order at the unmitigated 1h FVG under the green box "wouldnt be wrong if I did"; the trader's reason for skipping it (that losing the green box would weaken and invalidate the setup) is NOT a rule: "Don't copy me on last sentence". Sizing: tj size --add-entry. Fills: the stop sits beyond every order, so it is reached only after all of them fill: "it's impossible to hit SL when only 1 of 3 orders filled". R is counted on the full 1R: "if 1 order of 3 fills and reaches TP, for example 3RR it's going to be a profit of 0.9R (On trading we will count $ not only RR)" (trader, 2026-09-28). Leverage: one setting for every order, from the first order's stop: "our first limit order must not exceed 60%. if invalidation is 6% we can get 10X leverage. since we used 10X leverage on first order, we are going to use the same leverage on the rest" (trader, 2026-09-28).

entry_models.extreme_demand: Primary (long): at the extreme demand level.
entry_models.extreme_supply: Primary (short): at the extreme supply level (mirror).
entry_models.supply_level: Short at a supply level created by a bearish CH: sell limit at the unretested supply (T-0007), or the short on its first retest (T-0005, the level that created the reversal).
entry_models.demand_level: Mirror of supply_level: long at a demand level created by a bullish CH, on its first retest.
entry_models.reclaim: Longs when price reclaims a swept level or a demand it traded through and retests it as support; shorts mirror. T-0001: a swept level, used when the primary entry was missed. T-0006: a reclaim level + CH (the 4h demand traded through, reclaimed, and the long taken on its retest).

1.13.stop_model: Placed where the setup is invalidated. Longs: below the demand zone, the swing low, or a liquidity level. Shorts: above the supply zone, the swing high, or a liquidity level (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: at a liquidity level from the left that had been reclaimed as support. A return there means price reverses lower or goes into consolidation, and the setup is invalid. Not just beyond an obvious swing high/low: that is liquidity price sweeps before reversing, and the valid entry forms exactly there (trader, T-0004: "valid short position would be exactly on where I put my SL"). The stop goes beyond the zone that forms from the sweep (T-0005: above the new supply). T-0006: "placed SL on the last swing low it created" (51.02, under the Aug 2 sweep low of about 51.12). T-0007: "Our SL would obviously be our latest swing high in case level gets invalidated" (7,818.4, about 0.8 above the ATH that created the bearish CH). How close: "just very close to that swing point or demand/supply level" (trader, 2026-09-28): no fixed buffer. T-0006 about 0.10 under the low (0.18% of price), T-0007 about 0.8 over the high (0.01%), T-0009 about 0.0005 under the higher low (0.14%). The rule (trader, 2026-09-27: "yes exactly"): the stop goes a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH: a bit lower than the swing low for longs, a bit higher than the lower high / swing high for shorts. T-0006 and T-0007 are the examples. T-0004's stop sat beyond a high whose 5m CH the 30m never confirmed, so that high was liquidity. At liquidity levels (equal highs/lows, trendlines) wait for the break-sweep and the reclaim, then take the retest (T-0001, AAVE).
1.13.target_model: Opposing levels. "Both are ideal but it's more preferable to hunt strongest levels" (trader, 2026-09-27): the strongest opposing level (e.g. the next supply/demand zone; T-0006: the 70.70 supply) is preferred over the first level that gives at least 2.5R, which is acceptable. High R:R is hunted: 1:3 minimum preferred, 1:2.5 accepted. T-0006's order was 66.10 (3.41R): "I was happy with RR". T-0007: the key S/R level at 7,574 (4.12R).
1.13.risk_model: 1% of equity per trade, always. Fees are inside the 1% (trader, 2026-09-27); the bot will count them separately. No daily stop, no pause after losses, no cap on the number of open trades: "there's no stopping we stick to the plan. only 1% risk we ignore frequency. there's no pause" (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.13.leverage_model: Isolated margin. Leverage is chosen from the stop distance so that the loss on the posted margin at the stop (stop distance % x leverage) is 50-60%: "always aim for 50-60% at the stop" (trader, 2026-09-28), because "margin call occurs on 80%" (2026-09-27). Above 60% is a breach; below 50% is only short of the aim (the loss at the stop is still 1%). The aim is a preference, not a requirement: "its not necessary, the bot can use 20X leverage if invalidation is 0,6% for example (so total loss would be -12% it's absolutely fine with that, we don't have to reach it to -60% at all costs)" (trader, 2026-09-28). Liquidation must also sit beyond the stop: on tight stops the aim's top can liquidate first (0.6% stop: 100x is 60%, but a 0.5% maintenance rate liquidates first above about 91x; tj size prints the cap). T-0001: 3.14% x 10x = 31.4%. T-0006: 6.28% x 7-8x = 44-50.3%. T-0007: 0.615% x 20x = 12.3%. No fixed leverage cap: "with invalidation we can adjust leverage so we won't be close to margin call (80%). for example having 7% invalidation we can use until 7-8X" (trader, 2026-09-27). Leverage never changes the 1% risk.

management.invalidation: Stop at the invalidation level (see stop_model).

do_not_trade_when: Best target gives less than 2.5R.
The lower-timeframe CHoCH is not confirmed on 15m-30m (T-0004).
The entry would be at an inducement ('AVOID Inducements at all costs').

Price is in the middle of nowhere: no demand/supply level or key level at the entry, whatever the confluences. 'when we are in a middle of nowhere, it's more preferable not to execute. there wasn't any demand there or key level, even though there were confluences later on' (trader, 2026-09-28; T-0009).

A high-impact (red) USD event on ForexFactory is due within the next hour: no new entry, and resting orders are cancelled. Entries resume 1 hour after the release: 'they can resume after 1H after manipulation could stop. anything resting gets cancelled too' (trader, 2026-09-28). Open trades are kept (2026-09-27).
checklist: 1. HTF key level or supply/demand zone identified (4h): drawn from a CH, stronger with an FVG, fresh (unmitigated) preferred.
2. Liquidity swept into the zone (equal highs/lows or an obvious swing).

3. CHoCH by candle close, beyond the range of the impulsive candle that made the swing, read on the HTF (4H candle range): a break inside that range is NOT a CH, even if the 1h shows a pullback (T-0008). On the 30m: a close below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (shorts) / above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (longs); a 5m CHoCH alone does not count.
4. Entry at the zone (supply for shorts, demand for longs), not at a lower-timeframe CHoCH below/above it.
5. Stop a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH (beyond the zone too); never beyond a swing whose CH is unconfirmed, which is liquidity (T-0004).

6. Margin loss at the stop never above 60% of isolated margin (50-60% is the aim, lower is fine; split entries: the first order's stop sets the leverage for every order), liquidation beyond the stop, and best target >= 2.5R (3R preferred; the strongest level preferred).
7. No entry at an inducement: equal highs/lows are liquidity to be swept into the zone.
8. No red USD event on ForexFactory within the next hour or released within the last hour (new entries; resting orders are cancelled for that window).

1.14.timeframe_alignment: A lower-timeframe CHoCH counts only when the 15m-30m structure confirms it. On the 30m, a potential CH is a 30m candle that closes below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (bearish) or above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (bullish) (trader, 2026-09-27). Until then a 5m CHoCH is only 30m consolidation (T-0004: "the 5M CH was a 30M consolidation"). This is the candle-range rule (see market_structure) applied on the 30m. For a 4h zone executed on the 1h, the CH line is drawn on both charts (T-0006: about 56.00); the 1h is used only after the 4h shows a true CH (T-0008: "If there was a pullback and would see a true CH for potential short, we could jump to (2) 1H time frame").
market_structure: Lower low: a candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). A wick below without a close is not a lower low.
Higher high: a candle must CLOSE above the previous high (its wick).
Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
Bearish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE below the last higher low (mirror, confirmed). T-0007: after a new higher high, a lower low broke the previous higher low.

Candle range (4H candle range): price inside the range of the impulsive candle that made the high is consolidation. A pullback needs a CLOSE below that candle's low (above a bearish candle's high for the mirror). A break of a level inside the range is NOT a CH (trader, T-0008: 'to form a pull back from that price it had to break the lowest line and close below').

The candle range is read on the HTF first (4h): its high and low are the cyan lines. A lower-timeframe move inside it can be a 1h pullback, but it is not a 4h pullback; only a 4h close beyond the range changes the story, and only then may a trade be considered (trader, 2026-09-27).
Continuation in a bearish environment (lower highs, lower lows): after a pullback, a new lower low must CLOSE below the previous low including its wick; mirror for bullish (trader, 2026-09-27).
T-0001: the market was bearish; the 4H reversal (bullish CHoCH) was the confirmation, with confluences (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.14.trend_context: Counter-trend trades are graded like any other setup; they are just a bit riskier (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0007: short at ATH levels while the bias was bullish, "definitely worth the risk" at 4.12R. An FVG in the trend's direction between entry and target is a warning: price may close the gap or continue (T-0007).

"Both are ideal but it's more preferable to hunt strongest levels" (trader, 2026-09-27): the strongest opposing level (e.g. the next supply/demand zone; T-0006: the 70.70 supply) is preferred over the first level that gives at least 2.5R, which is acceptable. High R:R is hunted: 1:3 minimum preferred, 1:2.5 accepted. T-0006's order was 66.10 (3.41R): "I was happy with RR". T-0007: the key S/R level at 7,574 (4.12R).
1.14.risk_model: 1% of equity per trade, always. Fees are inside the 1% (trader, 2026-09-27); the bot will count them separately. No daily stop, no pause after losses, no cap on the number of open trades: "there's no stopping we stick to the plan. only 1% risk we ignore frequency. there's no pause" (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.14.leverage_model: Isolated margin. Leverage is chosen from the stop distance so that the loss on the posted margin at the stop (stop distance % x leverage) is 50-60%: "always aim for 50-60% at the stop" (trader, 2026-09-28), because "margin call occurs on 80%" (2026-09-27). Above 60% is a breach; below 50% is only short of the aim (the loss at the stop is still 1%). The aim is a preference, not a requirement: "its not necessary, the bot can use 20X leverage if invalidation is 0,6% for example (so total loss would be -12% it's absolutely fine with that, we don't have to reach it to -60% at all costs)" (trader, 2026-09-28). Liquidation must also sit beyond the stop: on tight stops the aim's top can liquidate first (0.6% stop: 100x is 60%, but a 0.5% maintenance rate liquidates first above about 91x; tj size prints the cap). T-0001: 3.14% x 10x = 31.4%. T-0006: 6.28% x 7-8x = 44-50.3%. T-0007: 0.615% x 20x = 12.3%. No fixed leverage cap: "with invalidation we can adjust leverage so we won't be close to margin call (80%). for example having 7% invalidation we can use until 7-8X" (trader, 2026-09-27). The only ceiling is the margin rule: "Ceiling should be 60% so we should avoid margin calls (80%)" (trader, 2026-09-28); no fixed leverage cap. Leverage never changes the 1% risk.

checklist: 1. HTF key level or supply/demand zone identified (4h): drawn from a CH, stronger with an FVG, fresh (unmitigated) preferred.
2. Liquidity swept into the zone (equal highs/lows or an obvious swing).

3. CHoCH by candle close, beyond the range of the impulsive candle that made the swing, read on the HTF (4H candle range): a break inside that range is NOT a CH, even if the 1h shows a pullback (T-0008). On the 30m: a close below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (shorts) / above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (longs); a 5m CHoCH alone does not count.
4. Entry at the zone (supply for shorts, demand for longs), not at a lower-timeframe CHoCH below/above it.
5. Stop a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH (beyond the zone too); never beyond a swing whose CH is unconfirmed, which is liquidity (T-0004).

1.15.timeframe_alignment: The CH comes from the higher timeframe first: "When we have HTF confirmations 4H-1D, For example a CH, we can jump on lower time frames eg 30M-1H and identify liquidity levels, RSI divergences, supply/demand levels and FVGs that can work in our favor" (trader, 2026-09-30). A CH that the next timeframe up does not confirm is a fake CH: T-0011, a 30M CH while "on 1H there's no CH, it was just a pullback on a consolidation range". A lower-timeframe CHoCH counts only when the 15m-30m structure confirms it. On the 30m, a potential CH is a 30m candle that closes below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (bearish) or above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (bullish) (trader, 2026-09-27). Until then a 5m CHoCH is only 30m consolidation (T-0004: "the 5M CH was a 30M consolidation"). This is the candle-range rule (see market_structure) applied on the 30m. For a 4h zone executed on the 1h, the CH line is drawn on both charts (T-0006: about 56.00); the 1h is used only after the 4h shows a true CH (T-0008: "If there was a pullback and would see a true CH for potential short, we could jump to (2) 1H time frame").
market_structure: Lower low: a candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). A wick below without a close is not a lower low.
Higher high: a candle must CLOSE above the previous high (its wick).
Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
Bearish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE below the last higher low (mirror, confirmed). T-0007: after a new higher high, a lower low broke the previous higher low.

Candle range (4H candle range): price inside the range of the impulsive candle that made the high is consolidation. A pullback needs a CLOSE below that candle's low (above a bearish candle's high for the mirror). A break of a level inside the range is NOT a CH (trader, T-0008: 'to form a pull back from that price it had to break the lowest line and close below').

The candle range is read on the HTF first (4h): its high and low are the cyan lines. A lower-timeframe move inside it can be a 1h pullback, but it is not a 4h pullback; only a 4h close beyond the range changes the story, and only then may a trade be considered (trader, 2026-09-27).
Continuation in a bearish environment (lower highs, lower lows): after a pullback, a new lower low must CLOSE below the previous low including its wick; mirror for bullish (trader, 2026-09-27).
T-0001: the market was bearish; the 4H reversal (bullish CHoCH) was the confirmation, with confluences (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.15.trend_context: Counter-trend trades are graded like any other setup; they are just a bit riskier (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0007: short at ATH levels while the bias was bullish, "definitely worth the risk" at 4.12R. An FVG in the trend's direction between entry and target is a warning: price may close the gap or continue (T-0007).

T-0007 (4.12R) was graded S; the avoided POL short (T-0008, 3.40R) "would be perfectly S" had a true CH formed.
grading.A: A good setup executed well, one step short of S. T-0001: "would be A because I missed extreme demand level but I got the reclaim support level ... it would be S if I would get extreme demand and get higher RR". T-0006: "would be A because I executed well but had to let it reach supply level so it would be an S". T-0010 (NEAR short, -1R): "setup was A even though it was lost": an A can lose.
grading.B: "B setup would be anything with decent RR but few confluences, which means it could be a risky execution" (trader, 2026-09-28). T-0009: "Setup B because of FVG ignorance but decent confirmations where could lead to good RR" (-1R). T-0011: "B, because we had good RR with LTF confirmation, but HTF was against our bias" (not taken).
grading.C: A setup taken without the full process, whatever the result. T-0003: "would be C because I focused only on 1M time frame regardless of win".

Macro news in the trade's direction: a red USD release that surprised against the asset (T-0010: 'CPI was higher than expected and it's bearish news'). zones.definition: A supply/demand level is drawn where price created a CH: a bearish CH leaves a supply, a bullish CH leaves a demand. It is stronger when the move also left an FVG. Trader, 2026-09-27: "we draw supply demand levels which form a FVG +CH". The zone is the level that created the reversal, not a sweep candle (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0005: the level that created the reversal left the new supply; the short was its retest. T-0007: the level that created the CH, close to the swing high, so it could also act as an inducement: that is why the stop went above the swing high.
zones.freshness: "A supply/demand level is high probability when it's not retested (mitigated)." "The more a supply/demand level mitigates the weaker it becomes." T-0001's demand kept an FVG that was not filled (trader, 2026-09-27). Unlike support/resistance, where more reactions make a level stronger. A zone that price trades through and then reclaims with a CH is a reclaim level, not a mitigated zone (T-0006: "there wasn't any mitigation, it was a reclaim level + CH"). T-0007's supply is the trader's mitigation example.
zones.extreme_demand: The full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: 85.61 to 88.05. Massive volume: the volume bar "exploded", much more than 2x; the trader asks not to focus on this (2026-09-27).
zones.extreme_supply: Mirror: the full wick-to-wick range of the high-volume candle at the higher high.

1.15.inducements: "AVOID Inducements at all costs" (trader, 2026-09-27). Equal lows/highs are resting liquidity (AAVE, T-0001: the equal lows were the inducement). There is no fixed tolerance for "equal": they may take longer to form and still count as a liquidity level likely to be swept (trader, 2026-09-27). Price is expected to sweep them into the zone: do not enter at them, and do not leave the stop just beyond them (T-0004: "I became the liquidity").

divergence.regular_bearish: Price higher high, indicator lower high: sell (T-0007: 7,793.9 -> 7,817.6 with RSI 81.1 -> 70.5).

divergence.hidden_bearish: Price lower high, indicator higher high: sell.
divergence.timeframe: Most timeframes work; the higher the timeframe, the stronger (trader, 2026-09-27).
divergence.reading: Swings on the RSI and on the chart are read on wicks. The RSI length is irrelevant (trader, 2026-09-27).

1.15.entry_timing: After a CH, the limit goes at the zone on the timeframe the setup is read on, the longer the better: "the longer time frame the better, the best example is T-0007" ("In that case, entry was on 4H chart"). Candle size after the CH is not a criterion: "Ignore small and weak candles" (trader, 2026-09-28). T-0006: the green box (demand) + the bullish CH were enough, "so I didn't have to jump to LTF". An unfilled limit is cancelled when price reaches the TP level first ("I cancel limit when hasnt filled when price reaches TP level", 2026-09-27). Front run: when price moves away toward the target without retesting the entry, the entry is cancelled: "we got front runned so we cancel our entry, since there wasn't any retest" (trader, 2026-09-30, T-0011). An unretested HTF FVG is a limit location: "considering a limit order there would be ideal" (T-0011, the 4H FVG).
1.15.split_entries: Optional. On the 1h or 30m, find extra unmitigated demand levels + FVGs and split the size across limit orders: "Usually it's going to be until 3 limit orders. 1 order only = 1% (Full size), 2 orders= 0,5% each, 3 orders= 0,3% (it's okay if it's 0.9% total risk) and yes SL and TP are the same for all orders" (trader, 2026-09-28). Supply mirrors. An unfilled order is cancelled like any limit when price reaches the TP first. T-0006: an order at the unmitigated 1h FVG under the green box "wouldnt be wrong if I did"; the trader's reason for skipping it (that losing the green box would weaken and invalidate the setup) is NOT a rule: "Don't copy me on last sentence". Sizing: tj size --add-entry. Fills: the stop sits beyond every order, so it is reached only after all of them fill: "it's impossible to hit SL when only 1 of 3 orders filled". R is counted on the full 1R: "if 1 order of 3 fills and reaches TP, for example 3RR it's going to be a profit of 0.9R (On trading we will count $ not only RR)" (trader, 2026-09-28). Leverage: one setting for every order, from the first order's stop: "our first limit order must not exceed 60%. if invalidation is 6% we can get 10X leverage. since we used 10X leverage on first order, we are going to use the same leverage on the rest" (trader, 2026-09-28).

entry_models.extreme_demand: Primary (long): at the extreme demand level.
entry_models.extreme_supply: Primary (short): at the extreme supply level (mirror).
entry_models.supply_level: Short at a supply level created by a bearish CH: sell limit at the unretested supply (T-0007), or the short on its first retest (T-0005, the level that created the reversal).
entry_models.demand_level: Mirror of supply_level: long at a demand level created by a bullish CH, on its first retest.
entry_models.reclaim: Longs when price reclaims a swept level or a demand it traded through and retests it as support; shorts mirror. T-0001: a swept level, used when the primary entry was missed. T-0006: a reclaim level + CH (the 4h demand traded through, reclaimed, and the long taken on its retest).
