required_conditions: CHoCH on the 4H in the trade's direction, close-based (see market_structure).
confirmation: Reversal on the 4H (bullish for longs, bearish for shorts)
Extreme demand level (longs) / extreme supply level (shorts)
Demand reclaimed after being traded through, then retested (T-0006)
Supply/demand level not yet retested: limit order placed at it (T-0007)
confluences: Liquidity sweep
Strong momentum + volume in the trade's direction
Inducement swept into the zone (equal lows below for longs, equal highs above for shorts). Never trade the inducement itself (see inducements).
Potential opposing level (used for the target)
Divergence at the swing (see divergence). A confluence only.
Fair value gap (FVG) left by the move that created the zone (trader, 2026-09-27).
Key S/R level with many reactions as the target (T-0007: the red ray at 7,574)

zones.definition: A supply/demand level is drawn where price created a CH: a bearish CH leaves a supply, a bullish CH leaves a demand. It is stronger when the move also left an FVG. Trader, 2026-09-27: "we draw supply demand levels which form a FVG +CH". The zone is the level that created the reversal, not a sweep candle (trader, 2026-09-27). T-0005: the level that created the reversal left the new supply; the short was its retest. T-0007: the level that created the CH, close to the swing high, so it could also act as an inducement: that is why the stop went above the swing high.
zones.freshness: "A supply/demand level is high probability when it's not retested (mitigated)." "The more a supply/demand level mitigates the weaker it becomes." T-0001's demand kept an FVG that was not filled (trader, 2026-09-27). Unlike support/resistance, where more reactions make a level stronger. A zone that price trades through and then reclaims with a CH is a reclaim level, not a mitigated zone (T-0006: "there wasn't any mitigation, it was a reclaim level + CH"). T-0007's supply is the trader's mitigation example.
zones.extreme_demand: The full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: 85.61 to 88.05. Massive volume: the volume bar "exploded", much more than 2x; the trader asks not to focus on this (2026-09-27).
zones.extreme_supply: Mirror: the full wick-to-wick range of the high-volume candle at the higher high.

1.9.inducements: "AVOID Inducements at all costs" (trader, 2026-09-27). Equal lows/highs are resting liquidity (AAVE, T-0001: the equal lows were the inducement). There is no fixed tolerance for "equal": they may take longer to form and still count as a liquidity level likely to be swept (trader, 2026-09-27). Price is expected to sweep them into the zone: do not enter at them, and do not leave the stop just beyond them (T-0004: "I became the liquidity").

divergence.regular_bullish: Price lower low, indicator higher low: buy.
divergence.regular_bearish: Price higher high, indicator lower high: sell (T-0007: 7,793.9 -> 7,817.6 with RSI 81.1 -> 70.5).
divergence.hidden_bullish: Price higher low, indicator lower low: buy.
divergence.hidden_bearish: Price lower high, indicator higher high: sell.
divergence.timeframe: Most timeframes work; the higher the timeframe, the stronger (trader, 2026-09-27).
divergence.reading: Swings on the RSI and on the chart are read on wicks. The RSI length is irrelevant (trader, 2026-09-27).
divergence.source: Reference chart the trader supplied to memorize, 2026-09-27 (four panels: regular and hidden, bullish and bearish).

1.9.entry_timing: After a CH forms, watch a few candles. If the candles are small and weak, place the limit order at the zone right away (T-0007); if price recovers strongly, wait (T-0006 waited for the reclaim and the retest). An unfilled limit is cancelled when price reaches the TP level first (trader, 2026-09-27: "Since a CH forms I wait few candles too see if they recover strong, if candles are small and weak I would place limit order right away. I cancel limit when hasnt filled when price reaches TP level"). The candles are read on a timeframe as long as possible: "the longer time frame the better, the best example is T-0007" (trader, 2026-09-28; T-0007 was read on the 4h). After a strong recovery (T-0006): "there was the green box (demand level) + the bullish CH, so I didn't have to jump to LTF" (trader, 2026-09-28).
1.9.split_entries: Optional. On the 30m, find extra demand levels + FVG and split the size across several limit orders whose total still matches the 1% rule: "I could do it on 30M to identify extra demand levels+FVG and split my size (example instead of starting of 1%, I could split it on specific number of limit orders so it could match the 1% rule criteria" (trader, 2026-09-28). Supply mirrors. Order count and allocation: open question 2.

entry_models.extreme_demand: Primary (long): at the extreme demand level.
entry_models.extreme_supply: Primary (short): at the extreme supply level (mirror).
entry_models.supply_level: Short at a supply level created by a bearish CH: sell limit at the unretested supply (T-0007), or the short on its first retest (T-0005, the level that created the reversal).
entry_models.demand_level: Mirror of supply_level: long at a demand level created by a bullish CH, on its first retest.
entry_models.reclaim: Longs when price reclaims a swept level or a demand it traded through and retests it as support; shorts mirror. T-0001: a swept level, used when the primary entry was missed. T-0006: a reclaim level + CH (the 4h demand traded through, reclaimed, and the long taken on its retest).

1.9.stop_model: Placed where the setup is invalidated. Longs: below the demand zone, the swing low, or a liquidity level. Shorts: above the supply zone, the swing high, or a liquidity level (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: at a liquidity level from the left that had been reclaimed as support. A return there means price reverses lower or goes into consolidation, and the setup is invalid. Not just beyond an obvious swing high/low: that is liquidity price sweeps before reversing, and the valid entry forms exactly there (trader, T-0004: "valid short position would be exactly on where I put my SL"). The stop goes beyond the zone that forms from the sweep (T-0005: above the new supply). T-0006: "placed SL on the last swing low it created" (51.02, under the Aug 2 sweep low of about 51.12). T-0007: "Our SL would obviously be our latest swing high in case level gets invalidated" (7,818.4, about 0.8 above the ATH that created the bearish CH). The rule (trader, 2026-09-27: "yes exactly"): the stop goes a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH: a bit lower than the swing low for longs, a bit higher than the lower high / swing high for shorts. T-0006 and T-0007 are the examples. T-0004's stop sat beyond a high whose 5m CH the 30m never confirmed, so that high was liquidity. At liquidity levels (equal highs/lows, trendlines) wait for the break-sweep and the reclaim, then take the retest (T-0001, AAVE).
1.9.target_model: Opposing levels. "Both are ideal but it's more preferable to hunt strongest levels" (trader, 2026-09-27): the strongest opposing level (e.g. the next supply/demand zone; T-0006: the 70.70 supply) is preferred over the first level that gives at least 2.5R, which is acceptable. High R:R is hunted: 1:3 minimum preferred, 1:2.5 accepted. T-0006's order was 66.10 (3.41R): "I was happy with RR". T-0007: the key S/R level at 7,574 (4.12R).
1.9.risk_model: 1% of equity per trade, always. Fees are inside the 1% (trader, 2026-09-27); the bot will count them separately. No daily stop, no pause after losses, no cap on the number of open trades: "there's no stopping we stick to the plan. only 1% risk we ignore frequency. there's no pause" (trader, 2026-09-27).
1.9.leverage_model: Isolated margin. Leverage is chosen from the stop distance so that the loss on the posted margin at the stop (stop distance % x leverage) is 50-60%: "always aim for 50-60% at the stop" (trader, 2026-09-28), because "margin call occurs on 80%" (2026-09-27). Above 60% is a breach; below 50% is only short of the aim (the loss at the stop is still 1%). Liquidation must also sit beyond the stop: on tight stops the aim's top can liquidate first (0.6% stop: 100x is 60%, but a 0.5% maintenance rate liquidates first above about 91x; tj size prints the cap). T-0001: 3.14% x 10x = 31.4%. T-0006: 6.28% x 7-8x = 44-50.3%. T-0007: 0.615% x 20x = 12.3%. No fixed leverage cap: "with invalidation we can adjust leverage so we won't be close to margin call (80%). for example having 7% invalidation we can use until 7-8X" (trader, 2026-09-27). Leverage never changes the 1% risk.

management.invalidation: Stop at the invalidation level (see stop_model).

do_not_trade_when: Best target gives less than 2.5R.
The lower-timeframe CHoCH is not confirmed on 15m-30m (T-0004).
The entry would be at an inducement ('AVOID Inducements at all costs').

A high-impact (red) USD event on ForexFactory is due within the next hour: no new entry, and resting orders are cancelled. Entries resume 1 hour after the release: 'they can resume after 1H after manipulation could stop. anything resting gets cancelled too' (trader, 2026-09-28). Open trades are kept (2026-09-27).
checklist: 1. HTF key level or supply/demand zone identified (4h): drawn from a CH, stronger with an FVG, fresh (unmitigated) preferred.
2. Liquidity swept into the zone (equal highs/lows or an obvious swing).

3. CHoCH by candle close, beyond the range of the impulsive candle that made the swing, read on the HTF (4H candle range): a break inside that range is NOT a CH, even if the 1h shows a pullback (T-0008). On the 30m: a close below the previous bullish 30m candle's low (shorts) / above the previous bearish 30m candle's high (longs); a 5m CHoCH alone does not count.
4. Entry at the zone (supply for shorts, demand for longs), not at a lower-timeframe CHoCH below/above it.
5. Stop a bit beyond the swing that created the confirmed CH (beyond the zone too); never beyond a swing whose CH is unconfirmed, which is liquidity (T-0004).
6. Margin loss at the stop 50-60% of isolated margin (never above 60%) with liquidation beyond the stop, and best target >= 2.5R (3R preferred; the strongest level preferred).
7. No entry at an inducement: equal highs/lows are liquidity to be swept into the zone.
8. No red USD event on ForexFactory within the next hour or released within the last hour (new entries; resting orders are cancelled for that window).
open_questions: 1. Entry timing: the candles after a CH are read on the longest timeframe (T-0007). How many candles is 'a few', and what makes them 'small and weak'? A test the bot could run: the next 3 closed candles on the zone's timeframe each have a body under half the CH candle's body, and none closes back beyond the CH level. Is that right, or what instead?

2. Split entries: how many limit orders, how is the 1% shared (equally, or more at the deeper level), is there one stop for all of them, and are unfilled orders cancelled at the TP like a single limit?

3. T-0006 is recorded as executed on the 1h (your chart 2: 'how we execute on lower time frames'). You now cite it as a 4h example that did not need the LTF. Was the entry decided on the 4h, with the 1h shown only for detail?

4. Stop buffer: 'a bit' beyond the swing was about 0.10 below the low on T-0006 (about 0.18% of price) and about 0.8 above the high on T-0007 (about 0.01%). How should the bot size 'a bit': ticks, a % of price, or a share of the zone's height?

hypotheses: Lower-timeframe CHs that the next timeframe up does not confirm fail (n=3: T-0004 taken -1R, T-0008 and T-0011 avoided, both -1R COUNTERFACTUAL).
Cancelling a limit after a front run avoids retests that come back with force (n=1).

review.lesson: A CH counts only when the next timeframe up agrees: a 30m CH inside a 1h consolidation range is a fake CH. definitions.label: Top-down
definitions.rule: HTF context, key levels, then LTF execution (timeframes.top_down)

definitions.label: Valid setup
definitions.rule: Setup valid under the strategy version (review.setup_validity)

definitions.label: Leverage
definitions.rule: Stop % x leverage at most 60% of margin (aim 50-60%)

definitions.label: Stop
definitions.rule: Stop respected: not moved, widened or removed

stages.name: 1. Specify the rules
stages.goal: Every rule becomes mechanical: a program reading it takes the same trades you do. Losses and shorts are required because a rulebook learned only from winning longs has never seen its failure modes.

stages.name: 2. Codify and verify the detector
stages.goal: Code that scans 4H OHLCV + volume finds the setups you journaled, with the same zone, stop and target. If the code disagrees with you, a backtest would test a different strategy.

criteria.label: Detector reproduces journaled setups
criteria.target: At least 80% of journaled setups found with matching zone, stop and target; every miss explained

criteria.label: Malfunction guard implemented and tripped by tests
criteria.target: Every check G1-G9 in malfunction_guard has a test that trips it and shows the block or repair and the incident entry

stages.name: 3. Backtest out of sample
stages.goal: Hundreds of historical setups are replayed with fees, slippage and funding. This is where the sample size comes from: manual trading cannot produce it fast enough.

criteria.label: Out-of-sample expectancy is positive
criteria.target: 95% CI lower bound of expectancy > 0 on held-out data; n from the sample-size table, never below 100

criteria.label: Result holds across conditions
criteria.target: At least 2 trend regimes and 3 assets; no single asset or month carries the result

criteria.label: Drawdown is survivable at 1% risk
criteria.target: Worst simulated drawdown and losing streak accepted by the trader before going live

stages.name: 4. Forward test without money
stages.goal: The bot runs live on the exchange's data and logs orders without sending them.

criteria.label: Forward signals match the backtest
criteria.target: At least 30 signals; expectancy inside the backtest's confidence interval; zero execution errors

stages.name: 5. Live at reduced risk
stages.goal: Real orders at a quarter of the normal risk, with every safety control switched on.

criteria.label: Safety controls verified
criteria.target: All items in `safety` below are in place and tested

criteria.label: Live results match the backtest
criteria.target: At least 30 live trades at 0.25% risk; results inside the backtest's confidence interval

stages.name: 6. Full risk
stages.goal: Scale to the normal 1% risk only after live evidence agrees with the backtest.

criteria.label: Scaled to 1% risk
criteria.target: Trader's explicit decision, recorded with the live report as evidence

sample_size.note: Trades needed so that, if the edge is real, the 95% confidence interval of expectancy excludes zero 80% of the time. Two-outcome model (every loss -1R), so real needs are somewhat higher.

safety: API keys never go into chat, the repository or kb.json. They live only in the bot server's secret store or environment.
Keys have trade permission only: withdrawals disabled, IP-whitelisted to the bot's server.
The bot trades a dedicated sub-account funded with only the capital it may risk.

Every order is placed with its exchange-side stop, sized by the 1% rule, with leverage set from the stop distance by the margin rule (aim 50-60% of margin at the stop, never above 60%, margin call at 80%), never above 20x, and capped so liquidation sits beyond the stop.

Trading rules have no daily stop, no pause after losses and no correlation cap (trader, 2026-09-27/28). The malfunction guard (G1-G9 above) is separate and mandatory: it blocks or repairs the one action only a bug produces and logs it; it never halts the bot.

Leverage: the highest whole number with at most 60% of the margin lost at the stop ('Ceiling should be 60% so we should avoid margin calls (80%)', trader, 2026-09-28), at most 20x ('we should stick to the maximum of 20X leverage for safety reasons', 2026-10-13) and liquidation at least 1.5x the stop distance away at MEXC's tier, capped by the pair's maximum; split entries take it from the first order. Lower is always allowed. On T-0011's 0.447% stop that is 20x (85x without the ceiling: a stop that slipped to the 15:35 spike would have been liquidated).
Macro release results (CPI above or below forecast) are the trader's call, not a bot input ('its actually my call', 2026-09-28): the bot only applies the news window.
Every entry and every exit (stop or target) sends a trade alert with the execution analysis, entry and exit prices, risk in USDT, leverage and setup type (trader, 2026-09-28).
No new entries and no resting orders from 1 hour before to 1 hour after a red (high-impact) USD event on ForexFactory; open trades are kept (trader, 2026-09-27/28). Otherwise the bot runs 24/7.
Execution is deterministic code, not a language model: the same market data always produces the same orders, and every decision is logged.

malfunction_guard.on_trip: Block or repair only the faulty order or position, leave every exchange-side stop in place, log the event as an incident (the terminal's Health tab) and report it to the trader as an error, explaining what happened. The bot keeps trading: no halts. Nothing is closed except by G1. Trader, 2026-09-28: "any issues are appearing, you mention them as errors, you explain to me what happened and we are looking for a fix. of course we don't halt but we keep an eye to minimize these types of mistakes or bugs".

checks.name: Position without a stop
checks.trigger: An entry order sent without an attached exchange-side stop, or a position on the exchange with no live stop order.
checks.action: Place the planned stop at once; if the exchange refuses it, close the position at market.

checks.name: Risk above 1%
checks.trigger: Size x (entry to stop distance) plus fees is above 1% of equity for the setup (all its split orders together; 0.9% for three), checked before sending and again on every fill.
checks.action: Refuse the order; if already filled, reduce the position to 1% risk.

checks.name: Leverage above the margin rule or the 20x ceiling
checks.trigger: Stop distance % x leverage above 60% of the posted margin, or leverage above 20x (trader, 2026-10-13: 'we should stick to the maximum of 20X leverage for safety reasons'). Split entries: the first order's stop sets the leverage for every order.
checks.action: Refuse the order; resend it only with leverage inside the rule.

checks.name: Liquidation before the stop
checks.trigger: Isolated liquidation, computed with MEXC's maintenance-margin tier for this position size, sits at or inside the stop, or (split entries) before the next order fills (warn under 1.5x the stop distance).
checks.action: Refuse the order; resend it only with leverage that keeps liquidation beyond the stop.

checks.name: Order burst or duplicate
checks.trigger: More orders in a window than the strategy can produce (limit set from the backtest's highest signal rate), or more orders for one setup than its split plan (at most 3 limits, one stop, one target).

checks.name: Order inside the news window
checks.trigger: A new entry or a resting order from 1 hour before to 1 hour after a red USD event on ForexFactory, or the calendar could not be read.

checks.name: Pair not on the scan list
checks.trigger: An order on a pair outside profile execution_venue.pairs.

checks.name: Bot and exchange disagree
checks.trigger: The bot's own record of orders and positions differs from the exchange's (unknown position, missing order, different size or stop).
checks.action: Treat the exchange as the truth: put the planned stop and target on every open position, cancel orders the bot did not plan, log the difference.

checks.name: Stale data or repeated errors
checks.trigger: Market data older than one execution candle, the clock off by more than a few seconds, or repeated rejected orders and API errors.
checks.action: No new orders until the data is fresh again (automatic); retry errors with backoff and log them.

incidents.title: A bare `no` in a trade record became the boolean false
incidents.detail: YAML reads an unquoted no/yes as false/true, so `strategy_change: no` failed with an opaque enum error instead of meaning "no change".
incidents.fix: The validator names the cause and says to quote the word (commit 6e7a0d6).

incidents.title: WebP chart screenshots were dropped from the terminal
incidents.detail: The image type came from the system MIME table, which lacks .webp on some machines, so those charts were silently left out.
incidents.fix: An explicit image-type table in the build, and the audit checks every embedded chart byte for byte (commit 490349a).

incidents.title: The report's mean holding time ignored stated durations
incidents.detail: Trades with fills.duration_minutes (scalps) were timed from their dates instead, so the mean was wrong.
incidents.fix: The report uses the stated minutes (commit 490349a).

incidents.title: The terminal header showed only the first strategy
incidents.detail: With two strategies recorded, the header listed one.
incidents.fix: All strategies listed (commit 490349a).

incidents.title: Leverage caps were rounded UP
incidents.detail: For T-0006's 6.282% stop the cap under the margin rule is 7.96x; tj size printed "8.0x" and then flagged 8x as a breach. A bot reading a rounded-up cap would set leverage that breaks the trader's rule. The same rounding sat in the validator message and in two places in the terminal.
incidents.fix: Every cap is floored to 0.01x by one formatter (risk.fmt_cap and the terminal's fmtCap); a test proves both agree and never round up (commit cd8ef0a).

incidents.title: The margin-rule note had 50% hard-coded
incidents.detail: The terminal's text did not read the trader's limit from the profile, so a rule change would have left the screen wrong.
incidents.fix: The note reads the profile (commit cd8ef0a).

incidents.title: Two numbered question lists were merged into one in Data gaps
incidents.detail: Questions from two strategies appeared as a single list with clashing numbers.
incidents.fix: Questions are grouped under each strategy (commit cd8ef0a).

incidents.title: Two JavaScript syntax errors in terminal edits
incidents.detail: An extra ')' in the excursion chart and an unclosed grid block. Either would have blanked the terminal.
incidents.fix: The script-parse and headless-browser render tests failed before the commit; both were fixed first.

incidents.title: The render test depended on the current number of trades and questions
incidents.detail: It would have failed on every new trade, training everyone to ignore it.
incidents.fix: The test derives its expectations from kb.json.

incidents.title: T-0003 duration recorded as the approximate 45 minutes
incidents.detail: The chart measures 24 minutes. The trader had said the 45 was approximate: 'you can fix it'.
incidents.fix: Corrected to 24 minutes with the trader's approval (commit 3d0e045).

incidents.title: T-0006 target recorded at 62.64 instead of 66.10
incidents.detail: 62.64 was the resistance named as a confluence; the order was at 66.10 (3.41R).
incidents.fix: Target corrected to 66.10; 62.64 kept as a confluence.

incidents.title: Zone readings the trader corrected: T-0006 'mitigated', T-0005 'sweep candle'
incidents.detail: The agent read T-0006's demand as mitigated (the trader: a reclaim level + CH, not mitigation) and T-0005's supply as a sweep candle (the trader: the level that created the reversal).
incidents.fix: Both records and the strategy's zone rules corrected (commit 23d6d55).

incidents.title: A duplicate key in the profile silently erased a definition
incidents.detail: terminology had `inducement:` twice. YAML keeps the last duplicate and drops the first without an error, so "Equal lows = liquidity resting below" never reached the terminal or kb.json. Found while editing the profile; a scan of all 38 YAML files found no other case.
incidents.fix: The two definitions merged; the loader now rejects a duplicate key in every YAML file, and a test proves it.

incidents.title: T-0004 loss typed D (invalid setup); the trader: good setup, executed early
incidents.detail: The agent classified the setup invalid. The trader: 'setup was good but executed early', which is a type C execution error.
incidents.fix: Loss type C, setup valid, entered_before_confirmation added, rescored; grade D recorded.

incidents.title: On tight stops the 60% margin rule allows leverage that liquidates before the stop
incidents.detail: Stop distance x leverage = 60% says nothing about maintenance margin. A 0.6% stop at 100x is exactly 60%, yet at a 0.5% maintenance rate isolated liquidation (about 99.50 on a 100 entry) comes before the 99.40 stop: the stop cannot protect the position. The limit is about 91x there, and MEXC's tiers raise the maintenance rate as size grows.
incidents.fix: tj size prints the highest leverage whose liquidation stays beyond the stop and warns when the 50-60% aim cannot be met; the terminal's Max leverage column is the lower of the two caps (it binds on T-0003 and T-0007); the audit re-derives it; malfunction guard G4 makes the bot refuse such an order using MEXC's own tier.

incidents.title: An unquoted version 1.10 would have been read as 1.1
incidents.detail: YAML parses `version: 1.10` as the number 1.1. Strategy versions are matched as text, so a trade tagged 1.10 without quotes would have counted silently under v1.1 and split per-version statistics. Latent: every current record quotes its version, but the next clarification of supply-demand-structure is v1.10.
incidents.fix: The validator refuses a numeric strategy.version, current_version or resulting_version; a test proves it.

incidents.title: T-0006 execution timeframe recorded as 1h; the entry was decided on the 4h
incidents.detail: The record followed the trader's chart caption ("how we execute on lower time frames"). The trader: the green box + the bullish CH were enough ("I didn't have to jump to LTF"); the 1h shows unmitigated demand levels and FVGs. The trade schema could not say "execute on the 4h, look at the 1h for detail": the validator wanted the timeframe chain to end at the lowest timeframe viewed.
incidents.fix: T-0006 execution 4h with detail [1h]; a new timeframes.detail field, validated to sit below the execution timeframe, with a test.

incidents.title: Two chart-read errors on T-0009, caught before recording
incidents.detail: The grey price-label box at the right edge of the 1h chart was read as candles, which put a false 0.4247 touch on May 6 (the 1h never went above about 0.394); and the first FVG fill check counted the gap's own closing candle as a later touch. Both contradicted other reads and were traced before anything was written.
incidents.fix: Label boxes masked, the FVG check rewritten on candle indices; the 4h and 1h reads cross-checked (same high and low for the Apr 28 15:00 4h bar).

incidents.title: Split-entry leverage was built on a case that cannot happen
incidents.detail: tj size --add-entry and bot question 5 treated "only the first order filled, then stopped" as the worst case and set leverage from it. The trader: "it's impossible to hit SL when only 1 of 3 orders filled": the stop sits beyond every order, so it is reached only through all of them. The margin rule belongs on the full position, and liquidation must be checked at every fill (the position has to survive to the next order). The old reading was never riskier, only lower than the trader's 50-60% aim (41% of the margin in the T-0006 example), and its CRITICAL flag fired on a stop-out that cannot occur.
incidents.fix: split_plan checks liquidation against the next order and the stop at every fill and reports the full-position figure; journal R for split trades follows the trader's unit (1 of 3 filled at 3R = +0.9R) in the model, the validator and the audit; tests cover both. The trader then set the leverage rule (2026-09-28): the first order must not exceed 60%, the same leverage for every order. tj size enforces it as CRITICAL.

incidents.title: The first outlook design would have shown +172R as the expected result of 100 trades
incidents.detail: Resampling only the 7 measured trades treats their 57% win rate as the truth: the median path ended at +172R with 0% chance of ending below zero. Seven trades allow a win rate as low as about 25% (95% Wilson bound), where the same average win gives +0.19R per trade and about 1 run in 5 ends negative.
incidents.fix: The outlook shows two scenarios side by side, as sampled and at the low win rate, and says it is a range to plan drawdowns against, not a forecast; the audit replays both.

incidents.title: An edit to T-0011 nested double quotes inside a YAML string
incidents.detail: Recording the trader's answer on the Sep 30 news put a double-quoted quote inside a double-quoted evidence line, which made T-0011.yaml unreadable. Nothing was committed or built from it.
incidents.fix: The validator's load check failed before the commit; the quote was rewritten with single quotes and every edited YAML file was parsed again.
